heading: Carrying a chain to another chain, and proving it later
lede: Bridging one ledger's history into another's is one of the oldest sources of real losses in crypto — a forged root, waved through because nobody on the receiving side could actually check it. HEZE's syndication is the same idea, built with the check included rather than assumed.

grid.p: Whatever a syndicate's doors signed since the last carry crosses at the interval, whether or not anything was ready — the checkpoint is taken either way, so a quiet interval is provable too.
Each syndication hashes the events it carried together with the previous checkpoint's own hash, so breaking one checkpoint without breaking every one after it is not possible.

The other world's chain arrives with orders of magnitude more volume than these doors did and reconciles without comment — not contempt, just scale, and the same scale is what keeps any one door from being singled out.

note.text: A checkpoint you cannot recompute is a claim, not a proof. Verifying a crossing means holding both chains and recomputing the source's own Merkle root at the exact sequence the checkpoint names — that is the one thing a forged root cannot survive, and it is the templated attack this design was tested against on purpose, not the one left out of the test suite.

text: Syndication taught through the real risk it addresses: bridging one ledger's history to another, and the recompute-both-sides check that a forged checkpoint cannot pass.
